text: P1 extracts the legacy reference versions, their rows and the lists of values the Workbench owns and hands them over through the published reference-data contract of rwb-case, which owns reference_version, reference_row and lov_value and loads, verifies and approves them on its own Flyway sequence. P1 keeps no reference table, no list table and no copy of a reference row in rwb_source_data. The rule rows and their test cases stay with the registry of rwb-decision, which this story neither calls nor loads.
why: The Ownership Map puts the reference tables with P3 and the rule registry with P7 while the legacy key and its three criteria are on the P1 slice, and DP-07 makes the rwb-case reference contract the only read and load path.
read: Ownership Map reference_version, reference_row and lov_value (P3); rule_row and rule_test_case (P7); context pack P1 ownership rows; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-04, DP-07 and DP-15; WP B2-P1-013 C dependency RWB-P3-E1043-CON
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Medium: one owner receives the extract and P1 loads none of the three tables.

text: No list that ACE holds is loaded by the extract. The action codes, the products, the branches and the holidays are read through v_ace_efs_action_code, v_ace_product, v_ace_branch and v_ace_holiday on the rwb_source_data login with SELECT only, and no row of them enters a file or a table.
why: Legacy AC1 forbids re-loading a list ACE holds and names the four views, and the reference table that would hold a copy belongs to P3 while the views stay P1's read path.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-014 AC1; TSD P1 v3 T3.3 views 10, 13, 14 and 15 (DF-ACE-128 to DF-ACE-130 and DF-ACE-146 to DF-ACE-159); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-05
confirm: Data steward and ACE team lead
impact: Low: the four views remain the only read path for those lists.

text: The reference data service of legacy AC2 is read as the reference-data contract of rwb-case: the verify operation returns the check result per row and per column, and the version in force answers with its row count, its content hash and its approver through the effective-dated list read. The rule-row half of AC2 is checked inside the file before the handover, where every rule row of a rule table carries the test case that proves it; the executable rule package and its registry remain rwb-decision's and no operation of rwb-decision is called.
why: Legacy AC2 names a reference data service that exists in no source document, and the WP fixes the contract dependency to rwb-case only, so the rule-row evidence has to be checked in the extract rather than through a second contract.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-014 AC2; RWB-P3-E1043-CON (verify and list read, version projection); WP B2-P1-013 dependency list; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-07
confirm: Data steward and solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Medium: one published contract replaces one unnamed service, and the rule evidence is file-local.

text: The ten clean days of AC3 are ten consecutive business dates on which the REC-01 to REC-05 reconciliation results of the date are all PASS with no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan, and on which the read-back of every version in force matched the file in row count, content hash, approver and valid from date. A BREAK result or a new orphan resets the count to zero. The sign-off is the data steward's signature in the cutover record of the release pipeline, and no counter table and no sign-off table is created.
why: Legacy AC3 requires ten clean days and a sign-off and no source gives the counting rule, the record that holds the count or the place of the signature.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-014 AC3; FSD P1 v3 A2.11 to A2.13; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 reconciliation_result and the REC-05 business-key rule
impact: Low: the evidence is read from results another story already writes.

text: The extract file format is one file per Workbench-owned table code, carrying the version facts, one line per row with its key and its data, the row count and the content hash, written in the load shape of POST /admin/reference-loads (file, table, validFrom, Idempotency-Key). The legacy tables stay read-only for the retention period their legacy retention class already gives them, and the records at go-live are served from rwb_case.
why: No source gives the format of the cutover extract or the length of the retention period, and the load operation fixes the transport shape but not the file content.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-014 AC1 and AC3; RWB-P3-E1043-CON reference-loads operation (multipart file, table, validFrom, idempotency); FSD P1 v3 A2.17 retention and archive rule
confirm: Data steward and solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Low: the format is internal to the cutover and the retention window is unchanged from the legacy class.
